4 Climate Action Climate change presents a multi-dimensional risk to our manufacturing operations in Financial Year 2025-26. Our facilities involve energy intensive manufacturing processes that are significant consumers of electricity and thermal energy, contributing to Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions. Physical climate risks including extreme weather events, flooding, and water stress can disrupt operations, affect raw material availability, and impact logistics networks. Transition risks are equally material: Tightening energy efficiency norms under the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), India's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), SEBI's BRSR Core assured disclosure requirements, and evolving environmental regulations all create regulatory and commercial adaptation imperatives for our business. Our OEM and ODM customers including large listed consumer durable and automotive brands with public sustainability commitments are increasingly embedding Scope 3 emissions tracking and supplier carbon performance criteria in their procurement frameworks. Failure to demonstrate credible climate action could risk our approved vendor status with environmentally progressive customers.

Our Climate Action Strategy for the Financial Year 2025-26 encompasses: • GHG Emissions Inventory and Reduction Targets: Systematic tracking of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions across all manufacturing facilities, with defined reduction targets aligned with BRSR Core disclosure requirements. • Renewable Energy Transition: Expansion of on-site solar power capacity and evaluation of Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) for green electricity, targeting reduced dependence on grid power for energy intensive manufacturing processes. • Energy Efficiency in Manufacturing: Implementation of energy management systems, variable frequency drives, waste heat recovery, and LED lighting retrofits across all facilities to reduce specific energy consumption. • Climate Risk Assessment: Integration of physical and transition climate risk assessments into business continuity and strategic planning frameworks, with particular focus on supply chain resilience for key raw materials. • Regulatory Transition Readiness: Proactive investment in R&D and capability adaptation to ensure our manufacturing processes remain aligned with evolving environmental regulations. • Supplier Engagement: Engaging key raw material suppliers on emissions reporting and energy efficiency to support our evolving Scope 3 disclosure obligations under BRSR Core.

5 Occupational Health and Safety Our manufacturing operations span a range of processes that involve inherent occupational hazards, including exposure to heat, noise, chemical agents, moving machinery, and ergonomic risk factors. Rigorous and sustained OHS management is therefore essential to protect the well being of our workforce and ensure operational continuity. The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 and its implementing rules have significantly strengthened OHS compliance obligations for manufacturing establishments. Our operations also involve substantial contractor and contract labour workforce engagement, whose safety management requires dedicated and structured oversight. OHS performance is increasingly scrutinised by our OEM and ODM customers as part of supplier sustainability audits. Any significant workplace incident can disrupt production commitments, impact customer confidence, and affect our standing as an employer of choice.

Our OHS management framework for Financial Year 2025 - 26 includes: • Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA): Systematic identification and risk-ranking of workplace hazards across all manufacturing operations, with controls implemented per the hierarchy of controls principle. • Behaviour Based Safety (BBS) Programme: Structured BBS observations and near miss reporting culture to proactively identify and address at risk behaviours before they result in incidents. • Contractor Safety Management: Pre-qualification, induction, and ongoing monitoring of all contractor and contract labour personnel to ensure consistent application of OHS standards across all workforce categories. • Periodic Safety Audits and Gemba Walks: Regular independent safety audits at all manufacturing facilities, complemented by Plant Head led Gemba walks to maintain visible leadership commitment to shop floor safety. • Emergency Preparedness: Maintained and regularly tested emergency response plans relevant to our specific manufacturing risk profile. • Incident Investigation and Cross Plant Learning: Root cause analysis of all incidents and near misses, with structured dissemination of learnings and corrective actions across all group plants to prevent recurrence.

Positive (from effective OHS management): • Reduction in Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) avoids direct costs from worker compensation, medical expenses, regulatory penalties, and production downtime particularly critical in high volume OEM supply environments where delivery schedules are tightly managed. • Strong OHS performance supports favourable outcomes in customer supplier audits, protecting approved vendor status with OEM customers who embed HSE standards in supply chain assessments. • A safe and well managed workplace enhances employee engagement, reduces absenteeism, and improves retention of skilled manufacturing personnel.
